findings.title: Paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
findings.body:
The PR null-guards `modelSupplier.get()` in `getSubGroupsCount()`, but three sibling methods do the same unguarded dereference:

- `getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max)` at line 256
- `getSubGroupsStream(first, max)` at line 262
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max)` at line 268

Each calls `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. In the same race the PR fixes (cached group still visible, row already deleted in the DB), `getGroupById` returns null. These methods then throw an NPE, which surfaces as a 500 on the admin subgroup and group-hierarchy endpoints. The fix should cover these paths too, e.g. by returning `Stream.empty()` when the delegate is null.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so exceptions can be missed and the thread leaks
findings.body:
After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty right away, without joining the reader thread.

- A request that was in flight during the final deletions can fail and append to the list after the assertion has run. That is exactly the window where the NPE race occurs, so the regression can go undetected and the test can pass while the bug is present.
- The thread outlives the test method and may keep issuing admin requests while the framework cleans up or reuses the realm for the next test.

Keep a reference to the `Thread` and `join()` it (with a timeout) before asserting. Also consider asserting that at least one read actually overlapped the deletions.

findings.title: If a deletion throws, the reader thread spins forever
findings.body:
`deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) only runs if every `remove()` call in the loop at lines 152-154 succeeds. If any `remove()` throws, for example a 500 or 404 caused by the very race under test, the flag is never set.

The non-daemon reader thread then loops indefinitely. It keeps hammering `GET /groups` for the rest of the test run, interferes with other tests, and can keep the test JVM from exiting. Set the flag in a `finally` block, or make the thread a daemon and bound its lifetime.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body:
The 100 groups are created directly via the admin API without `managedRealm.cleanup().add(...)`. Other tests in this class register their cleanup this way.

If creation fails partway (the `fail(...)` branch), or the deletion loop aborts, the leftover "Test Group N" groups stay in the shared managed realm. They can break later tests that count or list top-level groups. Register a cleanup for each created id.
